So far the discussion has revolved around the principles of privacy. I want to know if government spying and the mass collection of data can be quantified.

Does it significantly increase overall internet traffic? Is the NSA responsible for quantifiable negative effects on user experience? Curious if any technically-minded Voaters out there can put some numbers to it.
What might be the functional impact of government spying on our internet productivity? Can we put a number on the amount of bandwidth used to track our activities?

Does it significantly increase overall internet traffic?

No. Taps are placed at ISP core switches. Traffic goes in, traffic goes out. No increase in internet traffic because effectively, this is off the internet.

Is the NSA responsible for quantifiable negative effects on user experience?

That is a broad question. Negative effects? Sure. The knowledge of what they are doing may influence new startups not to buy server space in America. If you are talking about bandwidth performance, no. There are enough redundant switches that if a tap goes offline, another will pick it up.

Now, what I don't know is if the tapped traffic is fed back to the NSA's storage over commercial lines or on a dedicated line. If it's dedicated, no degradation of speeds. If on commercial, maybe a few ms, but I doubt it's anything noticeable.
